newsitem.title: DENMARK: Russian gas to N.Europe not seen before 2005-Gazum.
newsitem.headline: Russian gas to N.Europe not seen before 2005-Gazum.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, June 12, Reuter - Plans by Finnish oil company Neste and Russian gas giant Gazprom to bring Rusian gas to Europe through Scandinavia are unlikely to go ahead until 2005 or 2010, the managing director of a company jointly owned by the two companies told Reuters on Thursday.

Antero Jannes, head of Gasum which is 75 percent owned by Neste and 25 percent by Gazprom, said that Gasum was looking at two separate ways of delivering Russian gas to western Europe through Finland.
The first involves a line through Finland, under the sea to Sweden, and then south to Germany. The second involves a line from Finland under the Baltic Sea directly to the German-Polish border.
The first alternative would be partly financed by the European Union and the second is Gazprom's preferred route.
Jannes said a feasibility study was due to end next year after which a decision on the route would be taken. He added that a line would certainly be built, though not until 2005 at the earliest.
Jannes said that the cost would be several billion dollars but he did not go into further details.

"There are a lot of benefits to the Nordic Gas Grid," said Jannes. "Finland is the only place in Europe where Russia has a border with the European Union. Sweden and Finland both have room for their gas markets to grow. And gas production in the Barents Sea (north west of Finland) will start sooner or later."

But he said the main reason was that the European gas market was expected to continue showing explosive growth. "Production in Russia and demand in Europe make it very obvious that imports will increase. We need more lines to Europe," said Jannes.
Neste, the parent company of Gasum, is moving into the gas market in Britain.
"Only Britain has a gas business, but when the interconnector (linking Britain with European gas markets) opens next year, there will be a European gas market. We want to be a player," said Jannes.
Mahul Raval, formerly a gas broker with PVM, started at Neste recently and would be developing the gas business, Jannes said.

He added that Neste has no gas reserves in the UK sector of the North Sea, although it owned 7 percent of the Aasgard field in the Norwegian sector, as well as 5 percent of Heidrun and 12.3 percent of Brage. --Sebastian Alison, Copenhagen Newsroom, +45 33 96 96 50
